design: one generic policy across 10 unseen tasks. It starts the episode by whichever overlay exists, reads the goal sentence, and clicks the first visible element whose accessible text exactly equals a goal token, then presses #subbtn if present. No per-task code.

results.goal: Close the dialog box by clicking the "x".

results.why: needs a 3-level nested navigation, policy clicked only level 1

results.why: requires visual colour identification, not text matching
goal names no token to match

what_this_shows: live-geometry addressing is necessary but nowhere near sufficient

the binding constraint is the VERB SET: this policy has exactly one verb (click a text-matched element). Tasks needing type, multi-select, nested navigation, list selection, colour matching, or unlabelled targets all fail
a bespoke policy can solve a task that the generic policy fails (click-option: 20/20 bespoke vs FAILED generic), which is the definition of not generalising

relationship_to_previous_numbers.26/130 = 20.0%: measured earlier under a different policy and a different (hard-coded) addressing scheme
relationship_to_previous_numbers.2/10 = 20%: this round, generic policy, live geometry
relationship_to_previous_numbers.honest_conclusion: the project sits near 20% on unseen tasks whether or not geometry is read live. Fixing addressing removes a self-inflicted error but does not move the capability ceiling, because the ceiling is the verb set, not the coordinates.

why_this_is_the_important_number: it separates two failures the project had conflated: an ADDRESSING failure (self-inflicted, fixable) and a CAPABILITY failure (verb coverage, not fixable by remembering to re-read the DOM). The earlier 20% was mostly capability; this round removed the addressing component and the number barely moved.
